description: Na₄Zr₂Ge₅HO₁₆ crystallizes in the monoclinic P2/c space group. There are two inequivalent Na sites. In the first Na site, Na is bonded in a 6-coordinate geometry to six O atoms. There are a spread of Na-O bond distances ranging from 2.43-2.96 Å. In the second Na site, Na is bonded in a 5-coordinate geometry to one H and four O atoms. The Na-H bond length is 2.56 Å. There are a spread of Na-O bond distances ranging from 2.29-2.57 Å. Zr is bonded to six O atoms to form ZrO₆ octahedra that share corners with six GeO₄ tetrahedra. There are a spread of Zr-O bond distances ranging from 2.10-2.15 Å. There are three inequivalent Ge sites. In the first Ge site, Ge is bonded to four O atoms to form GeO₄ tetrahedra that share corners with two equivalent ZrO₆ octahedra and corners with two equivalent GeO₄ tetrahedra. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles are 40°. There are two shorter (1.74 Å) and two longer (1.80 Å) Ge-O bond lengths. In the second Ge site, Ge is bonded to four O atoms to form GeO₄ tetrahedra that share corners with three equivalent ZrO₆ octahedra and  a cornercorner with one GeO₄ tetrahedra. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles range from 35-53°. There are a spread of Ge-O bond distances ranging from 1.75-1.82 Å. In the third Ge site, Ge is bonded to four O atoms to form GeO₄ tetrahedra that share corners with two equivalent ZrO₆ octahedra and corners with two GeO₄ tetrahedra. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles range from 47-50°. There are a spread of Ge-O bond distances ranging from 1.75-1.81 Å. H is bonded in an L-shaped geometry to two equivalent Na atoms. There are eight inequivalent O sites. In the first O site, O is bonded in a 3-coordinate geometry to two equivalent Na, one Zr, and one Ge atom. In the second O site, O is bonded in a distorted trigonal planar geometry to one Na, one Zr, and one Ge atom. In the third O site, O is bonded in a trigonal planar geometry to one Na and two Ge atoms. In the fourth O site, O is bonded in a distorted rectangular see-saw-like geometry to two equivalent Na, one Zr, and one Ge atom. In the fifth O site, O is bonded in a distorted T-shaped geometry to one Na, one Zr, and one Ge atom. In the sixth O site, O is bonded in a 3-coordinate geometry to one Na and two Ge atoms. In the seventh O site, O is bonded in a distorted trigonal planar geometry to one Na, one Zr, and one Ge atom. In the eighth O site, O is bonded in a distorted trigonal planar geometry to one Na, one Zr, and one Ge atom.
